Go to definition, for a client that reads links: where what the cursor is
on is declared, with the range of what names it. Nothing for what nothing
is known of.

-- lib/dgdtools.yml --
root: .
driver_config: mud.dgd
conventions:
  call_registry:
    add_action: { function: 0 }
-- lib/mud.dgd --
include_dirs = ({ "/include" });
auto_object = "/sys/auto";
-- lib/include/std.h --
#define BASE "/std/base"
#define DAEMON "/sys/daemon"
-- lib/sys/auto.c --
void notify(string s) {}
-- lib/sys/daemon.c --
void register(object o) {}
-- lib/std/base.c --
int weight;
void create() {}
int query_weight() { return weight; }
-- lib/obj/a.c --
#include <std.h>
inherit base BASE;

void create() {
    ::create();
    base::create();
    weight = query_weight();
    notify("x");
    DAEMON->register(this_object());
    add_action("cmd", "x");
    call_other(this_player(), "cmd");
    sizeof(({ }));
}
int cmd(string s) { return s != 0; }
-- script --
initialize lib
open lib/obj/a.c

# inherited, however its path is written; a label to where it is given.
